criteria.name: Hook strength
criteria.notes: 204-char opener stands alone under the ~210 see-more cutoff, names the mechanism (supplemental deployment policy notice) and the news trigger (Sept 3 reopening, Sullivan's over-5,000 figure). Signals the missed-locations correction without snark. Short of 10 only because the correction framing is implicit.

criteria.name: Mechanism load-bearing + AK consequence
criteria.notes: Mechanism genuinely gates Alaska AI-connectivity capital. Names sector (rural connectivity/edge compute), decision (fund vs reallocate), actors (NTIA Administrator, GCI Holdings), and timeframe (this fall). AI nexus is concrete. Not a 10 only because the ~$370M is the desk's own arithmetic, honestly flagged.

criteria.name: Layer fidelity
criteria.notes: All three body layers appear in the dossier with controlling actors matching exactly (Commission/642, Assistant Secretary-NTIA Administrator/1702, GCI Holdings/GCI Liberty 10-K). No invented layers; FCC->NTIA->GCI chain is complete and readable.

criteria.name: Chokepoint clarity
criteria.notes: Names one specific layer (middle), the actor (the Administrator), and the binary (approve/reject/reallocate) under 47 U.S.C. 1702(c)(5)(C) and (g)(3). Asymmetric, 'a single desk, not a committee,' with FCC and state office explicitly placed upstream. Matches dossier chokepoint.

criteria.name: Structural read
criteria.notes: Explains what the vehicle produces and what it means for Alaska, grounded in the machinery ('the money gate is a single desk'). Position is present and proportionate but stays measured, largely deferring the stance to the closing question rather than stating it outright, so it reads slightly hedged.

criteria.name: Forward implication
criteria.notes: Names the concrete next move: map exposure to GCI's BEAD-dependent builds, treat the Administrator's approval as the gating binary, confirm the state's location list before the window closes. Trigger (Sept 3 notice) and window (this fall) given. Short of 10 only for lacking a hard date.

criteria.name: Primary-source quality
criteria.notes: All three dossier layers trace to genuine fetched primaries (47 U.S.C. 642, 47 U.S.C. 1702, GCI Liberty FY2025 10-K) and the chokepoint citation is a primary statute. But the operative instrument being anatomized, the NTIA notice itself, could not be fetched (503) and its terms rest on in-window news (Roll Call, Telecompetitor), which the body honestly attributes to Roll Call. Statutes prove the authorities exist, not that the notice issued or its exact terms, so the chain is strong but not fully primary at its core.

criteria.name: Voice match
criteria.notes: Analytical, structural, Alaska-first, business-literate, plain language ('the money gate is a single desk, not a committee,' 'on this desk's arithmetic'). No banned phrases, no influencer cadence, reads like post_001.md. No drift moment.

criteria.name: Readability (LinkedIn)
criteria.notes: Tight 2-4 sentence paragraphs, in the word and char window, one well-formed 3-item bullet block matching the three layers. Docked because the bullets run long and multi-clause rather than the single-clause items the top descriptor wants, making the block denser to scan on mobile.

criteria.name: Engagement question
criteria.notes: Closes with a real, debatable question tied directly to the chokepoint (should one officer hold approve/reject/reallocate authority, or does a remote build need a gate that can't close on a single signature). No CTA, no rhetorical softener.

one_sentence_fix: Convert the single-desk observation into an explicit stated position (e.g. name plainly whether concentrating approve/reject/reallocate power in one officer is a structural risk worth pricing) instead of deferring the stance entirely to the closing question.
